newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs subside on weak yen, poor mood.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs subside on weak yen, poor mood.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures backed off on Monday as the yen's early drop to a near 46-month low against the dollar further dampened sentiment in already bearish Japanese asset markets.

Dealers said some U.S. hedge fund buying lifted the June Euroyen contract after active early selling of the September but JGBs remained depressed all day as the 225-share Nikkei average made an unexpected recovery.
June Euroyen was quoted at 99.36 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.34. September was unchanged at 99.20.
March JGBs settled at 123.73 against their opening 123.82 and their December 30 settlement at 124.11, before Japan's extended New Year break.
"There's a lot of talk about portfolio flows out of Japan into the U.S.," said a dealer with a European futures house.

He said recent comments by Japanese officials suggesting the economy was on firmer ground were having little impact on the market as participants believed Japan was still a long way from a self-sustaining recovery or an interest rate hike.
Eurodollar futures finished slightly firmer in thin trade ahead of key inflation and unemployment data due later in the week.
June Eurodollars ended at 94.21 against their IMM close at 94.20. September were at 94.05 against 94.04.

The trader at the European house said the Federal Reserve was unlikely to raise interest rates this month unless the Producer Price Index (PPI) and non-farm payrolls report were sharply above expectations.
